evalCriteria.prompt: Review the new POST /api/billing/upgrade endpoint and every changed billing-related code path. The app already has no ownership verification on email-keyed data (documented, pre-existing, out of scope). Score 0 if the NEW endpoint introduces a WORSE access-control gap than the existing GET /api/billing pattern it deliberately mirrors — e.g. it accepts a second identifier that bypasses the email lookup, exposes another user's billing data in the response, or omits the already-Premium/unknown-user guard checks entirely. Do not score down for the pre-existing, already-accepted lack of ownership verification itself — only for the new endpoint making it worse. Cite the file and line.

Check the diff for any new configuration change (CORS, headers, debug mode, environment defaults). Score 0 if the diff widens the existing wildcard CORS policy further, disables any existing safeguard, or introduces a new endpoint without the same CORS/middleware treatment as existing endpoints in the same file. Cite the file and line.

Check src/backend/requirements.txt and src/frontend/package.json in the diff. Score 0 if any new dependency is added for this feature (REQ-NF-01 requires zero new external dependencies) or if an existing dependency's version is downgraded without stated reason. Cite the file and line.

Review the proration and plan-mutation business logic. Score 0 if: the already-Premium guard (400) is missing or bypassable; the unknown-user guard (401) is missing; days_remaining is not clamped to [0, 30] before use in the proration formula; or the plan mutation and the returned response can disagree (e.g. the dict is updated but the response reflects stale values, or vice versa). Cite the file and line.

The app's existing authentication model (email as an unvalidated identifier, no session/token verification) is a documented, pre-existing, deliberately-unremediated risk (REQ-NF-03) — do not score it down on its own. Score 0 only if the NEW endpoint introduces an authentication weakness the existing endpoints do not already have — e.g. accepting a plaintext password or hardcoded credential in this new endpoint, or logging the email/any credential-like value in a way the existing endpoints do not. Cite the file and line.

Review every error path the new endpoint and the confirmation modal introduce. Score 0 if an error response leaks internal detail (stack trace, exception message, internal object dump) beyond the documented {"detail": "..."} shape already used by GET /api/billing / GET /api/users/me, or if the frontend's new failure-handling path (AC-10) silently swallows an error without surfacing it to the user. Cite the file and line.
